label: The Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz
statement: Dated, sourced statements about the Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz, in aggregate: shipping, trade, supply, markets, reserves, policy and broad civilian and environmental effects. Each statement is as of its own date.
not_built: There is no open or closed flag and no current status: only what a named source said, and when. Nothing here identifies a ship, a port, a facility or a path, and nothing here enters an index, a count or a country's record. A market movement is never presented as infrastructure loss.
order: By statement date, newest first, then by id.
latest_note: is_latest_of_type marks the newest statement of its type by its as-of date. It is the most recent statement on record, shown as of that date, and older ones are historical. It is not a current status. Where several statements of one type share the newest as-of date, every one of them is marked and latest_by_type lists them all: none is chosen over another.

context_types.label: Shipping, in aggregate
context_types.definition: A dated statement that shipping in the region is restricted or disrupted, in aggregate.

context_types.label: Trade, in aggregate
context_types.definition: A dated statement about total trade volumes.

context_types.label: Supply, in aggregate
context_types.definition: A dated statement about total energy supply.

context_types.label: Market response
context_types.definition: A dated statement about prices or markets. A market movement is not infrastructure loss.

context_types.label: Reserve action
context_types.definition: A dated statement about the use of strategic reserves.

context_types.label: Policy response
context_types.definition: A dated statement about a government or international policy response.

context_types.label: Civilian and environmental effects
context_types.definition: A dated statement about broad civilian or environmental consequences.

source_roles.label: Operator
source_roles.definition: The company or body that runs the affected service.

source_roles.label: Government
source_roles.definition: A ministry, agency or official of a government.

source_roles.label: Regulator
source_roles.definition: The public body that oversees the sector.

source_roles.label: National cyber agency
source_roles.definition: A national computer emergency response team or cyber security agency.

source_roles.label: Court record
source_roles.definition: A filing or judgment of a court.

source_roles.label: Wire service
source_roles.definition: A news agency whose reports other outlets republish.

source_roles.label: News media
source_roles.definition: A news outlet reporting in its own name.

source_roles.label: Specialist press
source_roles.definition: Trade or technical press covering the sector.

source_roles.label: Cyber security firm
source_roles.definition: A security company reporting its own investigation.

source_roles.label: Dataset
source_roles.definition: A published data series or filing.

source_roles.label: Aggregator
source_roles.definition: A site that restates others' reporting. A discovery aid, never evidence on its own.

source_roles.label: Actor's own claim
source_roles.definition: A statement by a group claiming responsibility. A claim is not corroboration.

media.label: Web page
media.definition: An article, release or page on a website.

media.label: Dataset
media.definition: A published data file or data series.

media.label: Social media post
media.definition: A public post on a social platform. A medium, not a quality level.

link_states.label: Reachable
link_states.definition: The page loaded at the last automated check.

link_states.label: Redirected
link_states.definition: The address now leads to a different address.

link_states.label: Checker refused
link_states.definition: The site refused the automated checker. This does not mean the page is gone.

link_states.label: Not found
link_states.definition: The page was not found at the last check.

link_states.label: Error
link_states.definition: The check failed for a technical reason.

link_states.label: Deleted
link_states.definition: The post or page was removed by its author or platform. A corroborated claim stands.

link_states.label: Archived copy
link_states.definition: The original is gone and an archived copy is cited.

link_states.label: Not link-checked
link_states.definition: No automated check has been recorded for this address.

affected_qualifiers.definition: The source gives the figure without qualification.

affected_qualifiers.label: about
affected_qualifiers.definition: The source gives the figure as approximate.

affected_qualifiers.label: at least
affected_qualifiers.definition: The source gives the figure as a minimum.

affected_qualifiers.label: up to
affected_qualifiers.definition: The source gives the figure as a maximum.

source_date_bases.label: Undated page
source_date_bases.definition: The page carries no date of its own (a running timeline, an agency landing page). It is cited without a date and earns nothing for being reported at the time.

source_families.method: Direct fetch refused (HTTP 403) on every iea.org address tried; not worked around. Statements taken from media and trade press that report or reproduce them.
source_families.limitation: All IEA entries are second-hand. June, July, September and October oil market reports not covered.

source_families.method: Enumerated the 2026 press-briefing index (7 pages) by direct fetch and opened each briefing on the strait.
source_families.limitation: Briefings not filed: 6 March (seafarer deaths, overlaps 1 March; not opened), 9 June (opened, overlaps 24 April), 23 and 25 June (evacuation plan and its pause, which concern how ships would leave; not opened), 8 July and 16 September (attack condemnations; not opened), 6 November (Council, opened, overlaps 11 November). One briefing whose address names a ship was not opened.
Date and signatory count not confirmed; nothing filed.
Only the July move is filed, and as an intraday quote. The April ceasefire move was read but not filed because the page gave no settlement value.

source_families.method: One search each for the United States and Japan.
source_families.limitation: No entries for the Republic of Korea, India, China or European governments; no demand-restraint measures.

source_families.method: Fetched archive PDFs for March, April, May, July, September, October and the live November page; extracted PDF text locally with a small standard-library script.
source_families.limitation: June and August issues not read. PDF text extraction loses table layout; only sentences in running text were used.

source_families.method: Read the current index page and three articles.
source_families.limitation: Earlier index pages (March to September) not enumerated. The 30 April article on reserve releases was read but not filed.

source_families.family: UN system (UNCTAD, FAO, ITC via UN News, Security Council)
source_families.limitation: UNCTAD pages show no dates. FAO statements of 14 April, 20 May and 26 May and WFP's March assessment not filed. UNEP statement of 13 March refused the fetch (403).

entries.claim: The U.S. EIA said oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz increased in the third quarter of 2026 compared with the second quarter, "when flows were severely constrained following the onset of the conflict".

sources.derived_claim: Hormuz shipments rose in the third quarter of 2026 compared with the second quarter.

entries.claim: The IEA said in its monthly oil market report that the oil market was set to return to surplus in the fourth quarter of 2026, with crude inventories rising by 1.7 million barrels per day in October, and that attacks on shipping remained a downside risk, The National reported.

metric.basis: rise in crude inventories in October 2026 (IEA Oil Market Report, November 2026, as reported by The National)

sources.derived_claim: Reports the IEA November report: surplus expected in Q4; inventories up 1.7 mb/d in October.
The IEA report itself (not read: HTTP 403 on iea.org).

entries.claim: Al Jazeera reported on 14 November that a UN assistant secretary-general, briefing the Security Council on 13 November, described the present maritime arrangements in the Middle East as "costly, unpredictable, and unsafe"; the UN's meeting coverage records his warning that shipping volumes remained below pre-conflict levels.

sources.derived_claim: Report of the UN briefing to the Security Council on 13 November: maritime arrangements described as 'costly, unpredictable, and unsafe'.

sources.publisher: United Nations (Meetings Coverage and Press Releases)
sources.derived_claim: UN meetings coverage of 13 November 2026: the assistant secretary-general warned that shipping volumes remain below pre-conflict levels.

entries.claim: The IMO Secretary-General urged shipowners and operators to avoid commercial activity in the Strait of Hormuz that exposes seafarers to unacceptable risks and called on States to enforce maritime safety rules there; he said at least 25 seafarers had died since 28 February 2026.

metric.basis: seafarers who have died since 28 February 2026 (IMO)

sources.derived_claim: IMO Secretary-General's statement of 11 November: call to avoid exposing seafarers to risk; at least 25 deaths.

entries.claim: The U.S. EIA said it expected the Brent crude oil spot price to remain near $100 per barrel for the remainder of 2026, and that crude prices rose in October for reasons including attacks on shipping in the Gulf, constrained shipping capacity and falling inventories.

metric.basis: expected Brent crude oil spot price for the remainder of 2026 (EIA, Short-Term Energy Outlook, November 2026; forecast completed 5 November)

sources.derived_claim: November 2026 STEO: Brent to remain near $100/b for the rest of the year; reasons for October price rise.

entries.claim: UN News and Al Jazeera, citing UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO), reported in mid-November that shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remained below pre-conflict levels; Gulf News, under a headline crediting UKMTO, described traffic as "well below normal but not stalled" (its text does not attribute the phrase to UKMTO). None of the reports states the baseline period used for the comparison.

sources.derived_claim: UKMTO characterisation, as reported: traffic well below normal but not stalled, and below pre-conflict levels.
Reports UKMTO saying traffic remained below pre-war levels.
UN News live coverage of 13 November 2026: transits remain below pre-conflict levels, according to UK Maritime Trade Operations; no baseline period stated.

entries.claim: The U.S. EIA said global crude oil refinery inputs fell in the second quarter of 2026 following the start of the conflict, and rose in the third quarter while remaining about 5% below the same period of 2025.

sources.derived_claim: Global refinery inputs fell in the second quarter of 2026 after the conflict began and rose in the third quarter, still about 5% below the third quarter of 2025.

entries.claim: The Korean outlet Herald Business reported on 16 October that the IEA Governing Board, meeting the previous day, reaffirmed its commitment to continue implementing the collective action decided in March and that member countries agreed to accelerate the release of remaining volumes; it said members had supplied about 330 million barrels to the market so far.

metric.basis: emergency stocks supplied by IEA members so far under the March 2026 collective action (as reported by Herald Business)

sources.publisher: Herald Business (Herald Corporation, Republic of Korea)
sources.derived_claim: Reports the IEA Governing Board meeting: commitment reaffirmed; about 330 million barrels supplied.
The Governing Board statement itself (not read: HTTP 403; date not confirmed).

entries.claim: The U.S. EIA assessed that crude oil production shut-ins averaged 4.8 million barrels per day in September, down from 5.8 million barrels per day in August and from 10.9 million barrels per day at the peak in May, and said it expected continued volatility in crude oil flows. Its July outlook had put the May peak at 11.2 million barrels per day; the two are estimates made at different dates.

metric.basis: crude oil production shut-ins, average for September 2026 (EIA, Short-Term Energy Outlook, October 2026)

sources.derived_claim: October 2026 STEO: shut-ins 4.8 million b/d in September, 5.8 in August, 10.9 at the May peak.
September 2026 STEO: earlier estimate of 6.7 million b/d for August and 5.0 for July (later revised).

entries.claim: The IMO Secretary-General said "the situation in the Strait of Hormuz is unresolved" six months into the conflict, and that around 6,000 seafarers had been unable to depart the Gulf safely, although some crews had managed to leave.

metric.basis: seafarers unable to depart the Gulf safely since the conflict began (IMO)

sources.derived_claim: IMO statement at six months: situation unresolved; around 6,000 seafarers unable to depart.

entries.claim: The IEA said in its monthly oil market report that global oil supply had fallen well below demand for reasons including the disruption at the Strait of Hormuz, and forecast a larger fall in global oil supply in 2026 than in its July report, Reuters reported; the Reuters report put cumulative stock draws since the war started at 410 million barrels.

sources.derived_claim: Reuters report of the IEA August report: a larger 2026 supply fall than the July report forecast; 410 million barrel stock draw since the war started.
Summarises the same IEA report: global oil supply forecast to fall in 2026, partly offset by higher production from the Americas.

entries.claim: The International Trade Centre said combined export volumes of 12 products from the Gulf economies it studied fell 54% between April 2025 and April 2026, with LNG exports down 95% in volume.

metric.basis: change in combined export volumes of 12 products between April 2025 and April 2026 (International Trade Centre, reported by UN News)

sources.derived_claim: UN News report of the ITC analysis: 12 products down 54% in volume; LNG down 95%.

entries.claim: The IMO said its Council condemned attacks on civilian commercial ships in and around the Strait of Hormuz, stressed that any arrangement between the littoral States must guarantee the non-discriminatory and unimpeded right of transit passage of all ships, reaffirmed that passage through the Strait should remain free of tolls and charges, and asked the Secretary-General to work towards "a coordinated and sustainable return to unhindered navigation through the Strait".

sources.derived_claim: Outcome of the IMO Council's 137th session regarding the strait.

entries.claim: Al Jazeera reported that Brent crude futures for September stood at $76.48 a barrel as of 06:30 GMT on 8 July, an intraday quote and the highest since 23 June, after rising more than 3 percent, reversing a slide that had seen prices return to pre-war levels; the report linked the move to renewed hostilities between the United States and Iran.

metric.basis: Brent crude September futures, intraday quote as of 06:30 GMT on 8 July 2026, not a settlement (as reported by Al Jazeera)

sources.derived_claim: Brent September futures at $76.48 at 06:30 GMT, up more than 3 percent; reason as given by the report.

entries.claim: The U.S. EIA said that following a memorandum of understanding signed by the United States and Iran on 18 June and increased traffic through the strait, it had raised its expectations for global oil production. It assessed that production shut-ins averaged 8.3 million barrels per day in June after peaking at 11.2 million barrels per day in May.

metric.basis: crude oil production shut-ins, average for June 2026 (EIA, Short-Term Energy Outlook, July 2026)

sources.derived_claim: July 2026 STEO: MOU of 18 June, increased traffic; shut-ins 8.3 million b/d in June after an 11.2 million b/d peak in May.

entries.claim: Pipeline & Gas Journal reported on 7 July that the IEA, in its latest quarterly Gas Market Report, expected global natural gas demand to decline by 0.5% in 2026, and that natural gas prices in Europe and Asia had eased from peaks reached earlier in the year but remained well above 2025 levels.

metric.basis: expected annual change in global natural gas demand in 2026 against 2025, which the source calls the third annual contraction in seven years (IEA quarterly Gas Market Report, as reported by Pipeline & Gas Journal)

sources.derived_claim: Reports the IEA quarterly gas report: demand to fall 0.5% in 2026; prices eased but well above 2025 levels.

entries.claim: The IMO Secretary-General welcomed an agreement between the United States and Iran and said it would allow the IMO to advance its plan to evacuate the thousands of seafarers stranded in the area, cautioning that implementation would take time to ensure the necessary safety and security guarantees were in place.

sources.derived_claim: IMO Secretary-General welcomes the agreement and its plan to evacuate stranded seafarers.

entries.claim: City AM reported that the IEA said observed global oil inventories, including oil on water, were drawn down by 250 million barrels over March and April, or 4 million barrels per day, and called the disruption "an unprecedented supply shock"; it said global oil supply declined by a further 1.8 million barrels per day in April to 95.1 million barrels per day.

metric.basis: observed global inventories, including oil on water, 'drawn down by 250m barrels over March and April, or 4m barrels per day' (IEA, as reported by City AM)

sources.derived_claim: Reports the IEA May oil market report: 250 million barrel draw over March and April; supply 95.1 mb/d in April.

entries.claim: The U.S. EIA said the Brent crude oil spot price reached a high of $138 per barrel on 7 April and averaged $117 per barrel in April, the highest monthly average since June 2022, "as the de facto closure of the Strait of Hormuz tightened global oil supplies". It said traffic through the strait had largely been at a standstill.

metric.basis: Brent crude oil spot price, average for April 2026 (EIA, Short-Term Energy Outlook, May 2026)

sources.derived_claim: May 2026 STEO: Brent high of $138/b on 7 April, April average $117/b; traffic largely at a standstill.

entries.claim: The U.S. EIA assessed that Gulf producers collectively shut in 10.5 million barrels per day of crude oil production in April, up from its estimate of 7.5 million barrels per day for March, and assumed the strait would remain effectively closed until late May.

metric.basis: crude oil production collectively shut in during April 2026 (EIA, Short-Term Energy Outlook, May 2026)

sources.derived_claim: May 2026 STEO: 10.5 million b/d collectively shut in during April.
April 2026 STEO: 7.5 million b/d collectively shut in during March.

entries.claim: The IMO said its Marine Environment Protection Committee adopted a resolution on attacks on commercial shipping in the region, warning that they could cause "large-scale marine pollution" in the Gulf and adjacent waters, and asked the Secretary-General to monitor environmental impacts.

sources.derived_claim: MEPC 84 outcome: resolution warning of large-scale marine pollution; monitoring request.

entries.claim: The National reported that the IEA said, in a quarterly gas report released on 24 April, that worldwide LNG supplies had dropped sharply, and that each month without LNG cargoes moving through the region results in about 10 billion cubic metres of LNG supply loss.

metric.basis: LNG supply lost for each month without LNG cargo shipments through the region (IEA, as reported by The National)

sources.derived_claim: Reports the IEA quarterly gas report: LNG supply dropped sharply; about 10 bcm lost per month without cargoes moving through the region.
The IEA report itself (not read: HTTP 403 on iea.org).

entries.claim: The IMO Secretary-General told Member States and industry that "there is no safe transit anywhere in the Strait of Hormuz", and said about 20,000 seafarers on ships in the Gulf remained unable to leave, with water, food and fuel expected to start running short.

metric.basis: seafarers on ships in the Gulf unable to leave (IMO)

sources.derived_claim: IMO Secretary-General's briefing of 24 April: no safe transit; about 20,000 seafarers unable to leave.

entries.claim: The IMO Secretary-General said about 20,000 civilian seafarers remained on ships in the Gulf, facing shrinking supplies, fatigue and psychological stress, and that 10 seafarers had died in attacks on commercial ships since 28 February. He linked an evacuation framework for the ships to "preventing an environmental disaster".

metric.basis: civilian seafarers remaining on ships in the Gulf (IMO)

sources.derived_claim: IMO Secretary-General: about 20,000 seafarers on ships in the Gulf; 10 seafarer deaths; environmental concern.

entries.claim: UNCTAD said the Strait of Hormuz "remains virtually closed", with ship transits down by about 95 percent between February and March, and projected that growth in global merchandise trade would slow from about 4.7% in 2025 to between 1.5% and 2.5% in 2026.

metric.basis: fall in ship transits through the strait between February and March 2026 (UNCTAD)

sources.derived_claim: UNCTAD's second assessment: strait 'remains virtually closed'; transits down about 95 percent; trade growth projection.
Dates the second UNCTAD warning to 1 April and repeats the fall of about 95% in transits.

entries.claim: FAO's Chief Economist said disruption to trade through the Strait of Hormuz was a shock to agrifood systems globally, and that global fertilizer prices could average higher in the first half of 2026 if the crisis persisted; the briefing gives a percentage range without stating what it is compared with.

sources.publisher: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
sources.derived_claim: FAO Chief Economist's briefing: fertilizer prices could average higher in the first half of 2026 if the crisis persists; the range given has no stated comparator.

entries.claim: The IMO said its Council, meeting in extraordinary session, condemned threats and attacks against vessels and the "purported closure" of the Strait of Hormuz, asked Member States to keep water, food, fuel and other essential supplies flowing to ships unable to leave the region, and called for a provisional framework for the safe evacuation of merchant ships confined in the Gulf.

sources.derived_claim: Outcome of the IMO Council extraordinary session of 18-19 March 2026.

entries.claim: Al Jazeera reported on 16 March that Japan had begun releasing oil from its emergency reserves, the release having been announced that day in the government's official gazette, and that the Prime Minister had announced plans the previous week to release 80 million barrels from stockpiles amid supply concerns that the outlet linked to threats against shipping in the strait.

metric.basis: oil the Prime Minister announced plans to release from Japan's stockpiles (as reported by Al Jazeera)

sources.derived_claim: Japan's release began 16 March; plan of 80 million barrels announced by the Prime Minister.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (Japan)
sources.derived_claim: METI notice on the release of national stockpiles (not read: HTTP 403).

entries.claim: The IEA said, in an announcement carried by Hydrocarbon Engineering, that its 32 member countries had unanimously agreed to make 400 million barrels of oil from their emergency reserves available to the market, to address disruptions in oil markets stemming from the war in the Middle East; the announcement's headline called it the largest ever oil stock release. The U.S. Department of Energy said on 11 March that the agreement had been reached earlier that day.

metric.basis: oil from emergency reserves that IEA member countries agreed to make available to the market (IEA announcement as carried by Hydrocarbon Engineering; agreement dated 11 March 2026 by the U.S. Department of Energy)

sources.derived_claim: Carries the IEA announcement: 32 members agreed unanimously to release 400 million barrels.
States that on 11 March the 32 IEA member nations unanimously agreed to a coordinated release of 400 million barrels.
The IEA's own announcement (not read: HTTP 403).

entries.claim: The IEA said, in an announcement carried by Hydrocarbon Engineering, that the conflict had impeded oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz and that export volumes of crude and refined products were far below pre-conflict levels; the announcement does not define the pre-conflict baseline. It said an average of 20 million barrels per day of crude oil and oil products transited the strait in 2025, around 25% of the world's seaborne oil trade.

sources.derived_claim: Carries the IEA statement that export volumes were far below pre-conflict levels, and the 2025 transit baseline.

entries.claim: The United Nations said the Security Council adopted resolution 2817 (2026) by 13 votes in favour to none against, with two abstentions; among other things the resolution demands that Iran halt its threats, provocations and actions aimed at interfering with maritime trade.

sources.publisher: United Nations (Meetings Coverage and Press Releases)
sources.derived_claim: UN press release on the adoption of resolution 2817 (2026): vote and the demand concerning maritime trade.

entries.claim: The U.S. Department of Energy said the United States would release 172 million barrels of oil from its national emergency oil reserve as its part of the IEA action, beginning the following week and taking about 120 days to deliver.

metric.basis: oil to be released from the U.S. national emergency oil reserve (U.S. Department of Energy)

sources.derived_claim: DOE announcement of a 172 million barrel release over about 120 days.
AP report of the same announcement: 172 million barrels, about 120 days.

entries.claim: The U.S. EIA said in its March 2026 Short-Term Energy Outlook that the Brent crude oil spot price had risen sharply following the onset of military action in the Middle East, and that crude oil prices had risen as petroleum shipments through the Strait of Hormuz had fallen. It said that as of 9 March, when it finalised its forecast, the strait was "effectively closed to most shipping traffic".

sources.derived_claim: March 2026 STEO: Brent settled at $94/b on 9 March; strait effectively closed to most shipping traffic as of 9 March.

entries.claim: UNCTAD said military escalation had disrupted shipping flows through the Strait of Hormuz, which carries around one quarter of global seaborne oil trade, and that around one third of global seaborne fertilizer trade passes through it. It said freight rates for oil shipping and war-risk insurance premiums were surging.

sources.derived_claim: UNCTAD media alert of 10 March 2026 on its rapid analysis: shares of seaborne oil and fertilizer trade; freight and insurance costs surging.
Reports the release of the UNCTAD analysis on 10 March and repeats the one-third fertilizer figure (about 16 million tonnes).

entries.claim: The IMO Secretary-General, in a statement on the situation in the Strait of Hormuz, said he was deeply concerned by reports of at least one fatality and several seafarers injured in attacks on merchant vessels, urged shipping companies to exercise maximum caution and said that, where possible, vessels should avoid transiting the affected region until conditions improve.

sources.derived_claim: IMO Secretary-General's first statement: advice to avoid transiting the affected region; at least one fatality reported.
